analysis:
Changes: (1) api.py adds a dev-branch source gate (L73-80). It requires a push event, ref refs/heads/dev and RELEASE_ENVIRONMENT=dev, then verifies a GitHub-verified commit on dev ancestry. Tag, master-staging and dispatch paths are kept, and a master branch push now means staging only. (2) check-release-version.sh changes comments only; the regex is unchanged. (3) provider-release.md moves dev publication to release-dev-branch.yml and keeps master pushes to staging. It documents the staging lane, the identity table, dev ranking quirks and the APNs/keychain/model-cache sharing limits between dev and prod installs. (4) resolve-provider-release.sh has only a metadata/patch excerpt, with no full text. The patch shows master pushes limited to staging, dev pushes limited to dev, and prod refused on any branch push.

Security conclusion: the main regression is that unreviewed `dev` content now gets the production Developer ID signature and notarization. The docs admit review is not enforced on dev and defer the fix to an admin (see finding). The registration/publication secrets stay environment-scoped (DEV_* only), and the release path still gates production on a signed tag in master ancestry. A dev build's CodeDirectory hash should not match production-qualified builds, so App Attest and registry qualification (T-054) should still reject it on the production platform. I could not verify this because the platform code is out of scope.

Not verified: release-dev-branch.yml, release-provider.yml, the full resolve-provider-release.sh, and whether the `secrets: inherit` guards actually keep PROD_* secrets empty on dev. The next pass should confirm that a workflow file modified on `dev` cannot read the PROD_* secrets or reach the prod environment. Dev and prod sharing the same bundle id, keychain access group and APNs topic is documented as a known limitation, not newly analyzed.

findings.detail: verify_workflow_source now accepts any push to refs/heads/dev when RELEASE_ENVIRONMENT=dev. verify_source(..., "dev") only checks that the commit has a GitHub-verified signature and is an ancestor of dev's head. That proves a signature exists, not that anyone reviewed the code. The updated docs (provider-release.md ~L542-546) say review is not enforced on `dev`. They also say a dev build gets the same Developer ID signature and meets the self-updater's production designated requirement (~L296-301, ~L516-518). The reusable workflow runs with `secrets: inherit`, with Apple signing, notarization and provisioning-profile secrets in the signing job. Previously, signed output came only from reviewed master ancestry or a signed tag. A writer with push access to `dev`, or a compromised account with a verified signing key, can have arbitrary provider code or workflow changes signed and notarized under team SLDQ2GJ6TL and bundle id io.darkbloom.provider. The result is a notarized binary with the production bundle id, access group and APNs topic, which can be distributed outside the intended dev lane. Fix: before enabling this path, require a pull_request and review rule on `dev` (the doc defers this to an admin) or make the gate fail unless such a rule is present. Also restrict the dev-branch workflow's access to signing secrets, for example through a protected environment.
findings.title: Unreviewed `dev` branch pushes can now obtain production Developer ID signing and notarization
